proof_summary: Specializing to \(k=2\) and expanding \(\binom n2\) and \(\binom{n+2}2\) shows that every term of the second series is \(16=(2!)^4\) times the corresponding term of the first. The first series converges and has a positive term (hence a positive sum), so the claimed equality would force \(S=16S\) with \(S>0\), a contradiction.
